newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish dealers split on NBP intervention prospects.
newsitem.headline: Polish dealers split on NBP intervention prospects.

text.p: Polish forex market dealers are divided on the prospects of National Bank of Poland (NBP) currency buying intervention this week, as such a move would spark more foreign interest in Polish treasuries.
But dealers said the NBP has often intervened when the local unit was more than three percent from the parity rate. On Tuesday the zloty finished around 3.15 percent from parity.

"It is not clear whether the central bank will intervene as such a move would make Polish T-bills even more attractive for foreigners. The odds are now 50-50," said Witold Wozniak, forex dealer at Deutsche Bank Polska SA.

The central bank has often said that it planned to keep the zloty, traded within a 14 percent daily band around a central parity rate, volatile in the short-term to discourage speculative foreign capital flows.
Other dealers said the central bank would intervene on Wednesday if the zloty tried to strengthen further amid foreign buying of Polish treasuries and investment inflows.
"If the zloty gains more ground tomorrow we may very well see an intervention," said Karol Zaluski of ING Bank in Warsaw.
Dealers said the zloty would be under additional upward pressure on Wednesday as banks shorten currency exposure to hold higher-yielding zloty positions over the week-end.
The zloty closed at 3.17/3.13 percent from the trading band centre, stronger than Monday's close at 3.07/3.03 percent.
It closed at 3.1070/80 to the dollar, down from 3.0968/78 on Monday and at 1.8120/30 to the mark, up from 1.8191/01.

Dealers said that on Tuesday the zloty remained locked under strong resistance at 3.1 percent from parity until about 1200 GMT, when players decided that the central bank would not intervene with currency purchases for the rest of the day.

The zloty's charge on Tuesday was caused by foreign investor involvement in Monday's T-bill auction at which they bought an estimated $100 million as well as their entry into short-term bills in secondary trade on Tuesday.

"Foreigners were interested in buying two-month paper on Tuesday, but it's like walking on pins and needles because the forex market is wary of central bank action," said Wojciech Kowalczyk, senior dealer at Bank Handlowy SA.
Dealers said foreigners would again bid for large amounts of Polish T-bills on Thursday, when the Treasury will hold an additional 500 million zloty tender of 52-week T-bills.
Some players said the months-long rise in Polish T-bill yields had likely ended and that the Treasury opted to hold the extra auction to show that yields had stopped their climb.
